dedupe_keys.name: murray darling basin irrigation efficiency projects independent review of water savings and return flows

description: This article summarises an independent review, commissioned by the Murray-Darling Basin Authority, of every irrigation efficiency project funded in the basin, written after claims that water returned to the environment had been overstated. The Commonwealth committed A$3.1 billion to buy water rights, A$2.5 billion spent, and over A$8 billion to modernise infrastructure, over A$4 billion spent, aiming to save 2,750 gigalitres of surface water. The reviewers built a framework for return flows, the water that reaches rivers again through groundwater after irrigation, and found investment had achieved 85 percent of the 750 gigalitre a year target because reduced return flows of 121 gigalitres a year offset savings. Coverage: one basin, projects funded to 2019. Access: a free web article; the licence is not stated. Caveats: a summary of the review, not the report, and groundwater return flows are hard to measure. It supports irrigation investment appraisal and water recovery optimisation, and relates to the Bureau of Meteorology Murray-Darling Basin water information data in the catalogue.
